title: Rashid Khan and Wife Layloma Host Pathan Brothers for a Lavish Afghan Feast in Dubai
excerpt: Irfan Pathan called it "the most incredible Afghan feast," praising Rashid Khan and Layloma's hospitality in an X post that deepened one of cricket's warmest cross-border friendships.
body:
• Afghanistan star Rashid Khan and his wife Layloma hosted former India all-rounders Irfan Pathan and Yusuf Pathan for an elaborate Afghan feast at their Dubai residence.
  • Irfan Pathan posted on X on October 9 that it was "the most incredible Afghan feast," writing that every dish had its own unique flavour and he was "still thinking the food."
  • The dinner deepens one of cricket's warmest cross-border friendships — Irfan has long been Afghanistan cricket's most vocal supporter in India, famously dancing with Rashid after their 2023 World Cup win over Pakistan.

Rashid Khan cooked up more than dinner this week. The Afghanistan leg-spinner and his wife Layloma hosted former India all-rounders Irfan Pathan and Yusuf Pathan at their Dubai residence, laying out what Irfan called "the most incredible Afghan feast."

Posting on X on October 9, Irfan praised the hosts — "What hosts @rashidkhan_19 & Layloma Bhabhi are!" — writing that every dish had its own unique flavour, but what made the evening special was the love and warmth behind it. He shared a photo posing with Rashid and Yusuf, plus a video of Rashid personally preparing a plate of food for him. Two days on, he admitted, he was "still thinking the food."

A friendship beyond the boundary

The dinner is the latest chapter in one of cricket's most genuine cross-border friendships. Irfan Pathan has been Afghanistan cricket's loudest cheerleader in India for years — a bond sealed at the 2023 ODI World Cup in Chennai, when he kept a promise to dance with Rashid after Afghanistan's historic eight-wicket win over Pakistan, their first-ever ODI victory against their arch-rivals. The clip of the two dancing became one of the tournament's defining images.

Irfan's affection for the Afghan team ran through that World Cup: he celebrated their wins over Sri Lanka and the Netherlands with equal enthusiasm, and hosted the Afghanistan squad for dinner in Mumbai during the tournament. Rashid, now one of world cricket's biggest T20 stars, has returned the warmth ever since.

The food: what an Afghan feast means

An Afghan feast is a serious undertaking. The cuisine's centrepieces — kabuli pulao with sweetened carrots and raisins, slow-cooked qabili, seekh kebabs, mantu dumplings, aushak, and firni or sheer khurma to finish — are built for exactly this kind of hospitality: large platters, shared eating, and hosts who measure the evening's success by how much the guests protest they cannot eat another bite. Irfan's note that every dish "had its own unique flavour" suggests a spread that honoured the full range.

For food-curious readers: Dubai is arguably the best city outside Afghanistan to eat Afghan food, with a large Afghan diaspora running restaurants across Deira and beyond. If Rashid's home cooking has you inspired, the restaurant version — kabuli pulao and chapli kebab — travels well.

Diaspora angle

The image of an Afghan star hosting two Indian legends in Dubai is the diaspora's cricket in miniature: the Gulf as the neutral ground where South Asian cricket's friendships actually live. For Afghan and Indian fans abroad, it is a reminder that the sport's fiercest on-field rivalries coexist with its warmest off-field bonds.

What's next

Rashid remains at the heart of Afghanistan's white-ball plans, and the Pathan brothers remain fixtures of Indian cricket's commentariat. The next time they meet will likely be with microphones on — but the dinner table, as ever, did the real talking first.
